title: Zeeman Shift and Injection Currents under Light Irradiation
authors: Ruizhi Dong, Yihua Xiao, Pengfei Wang, Ruixiang Fei
abstract: The conversion of light into electrical currents enables energy harvesting and photodetection. Conventional second-order dc photocurrents are driven by the electric component of light through electric-dipole coupling and require broken inversion symmetry. Here, we show that the electric and magnetic components of light jointly generate Zeeman shift and injection currents. Using quantum perturbation theory, we derive explicit microscopic expressions for their conductivity tensors. We systematically classify the symmetry constraints on these responses and show how they differ from those governing conventional photocurrents. In particular, both responses can occur in centrosymmetric systems with spin-orbit coupling or noncollinear magnetic order, irrespective of time-reversal symmetry. A centrosymmetric kagome model exhibits broadband responses. First-principles calculations for Mn$_3$Sn further predict Zeeman injection and shift current densities of $10^{2}$-$10^{3}~\mathrm{A/m^{2}}$ and $1$-$10~\mathrm{A/m^{2}}$, respectively, under illumination with an electric-field amplitude $E=10^{4}~\mathrm{V/m}$. These magnitudes place both currents within experimental reach.
summary: This paper theoretically derives and analyzes Zeeman shift and injection currents generated when light couples both electric and magnetic fields. The key finding is that these novel currents can be finite in centrosymmetric materials, bypassing symmetry restrictions that forbid conventional photocurrents. This offers a powerful, measurable method for electrically probing magnetic order in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the generation of novel dc photocurrents—Zeeman shift and injection currents—arising from the joint coupling of the electric and magnetic components of incident light.
main_result: These Zeeman photocurrents can persist and be significant even in centrosymmetric materials where conventional electric-dipole photocurrents are symmetry-forbidden, opening a new pathway for electrical detection of magnetic order.
method: The authors employ quantum perturbation theory and density-matrix formalism to derive explicit microscopic expressions for the relevant conductivity tensors.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general systems, demonstrated using a kagome model with antiferromagnetic order and calculated for the specific magnetic material Mn3Sn.

main_assumptions: The analysis operates in the weak-coupling limit and assumes the dc response is dominated by the resonant interference term ($	ext{W}_{EB}$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the photocurrent generation mechanism, contrasting the vanishing EE term in centrosymmetric systems with the finite EB interference term, and show the calculated energy dependence of the Zeeman currents for Mn3Sn.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using perturbation theory, then performs a detailed symmetry analysis comparing conventional vs. Zeeman responses, and finally applies these findings to model systems like the kagome lattice and Mn3Sn.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, symmetry-based theoretical framework for accessing spin-dependent transport properties using light, which is highly relevant for understanding light-matter interactions in magnetic quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Fermi’s golden rule picture of photocurrent gen- eration in a centrosymmetric system. (a) For electric-dipole (EE) transitions, the inversion-even rate WEE and inversion- odd shift vector R or velocity difference ∆yield opposite con- tributions at ±k, giving JEE = 0. (b) The electric-dipole– Zeeman (EB) interference term is inversion odd, WEB(k) = −WEB(−k). The corresponding photocurrent contributions at ±k therefore add, allowing a finite JEB.
